texts.preamble: Rajesh Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 September, 2019 Author: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava Bench: Rajendra Kumar Srivastava 1 Mcrc-39678-2019 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-39678-2019 (Rajesh Gupta Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 1 Jabalpur, Dated : 24-09-2019
texts.facts: This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 0197/2019 registered at Police Station Industrial Area Satlapur, district Raisen (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of IPC. As per prosecution case in short is that on 08.08.2019, Food Safety Officer, Raisen has filed an application before police Station Industrial Area Satlapur stating that under instruction of Collector, on 27.07.2019, complainant along with members of constituted inquiry committee went to M/s National Industries for inspection. The inquiry officers have taken samples of ghee, butter, milk powder and pulp of custard apple (sheetafal). On examination, the sample of ghee is found below standard. It is further contended in application that Collector has directed to register the case against the applicant and Supervisor of Industry for the offences under Sections 272, 273 and 420 of IPC in addition to provision of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case. The co-accused Ganesh Yadav has already been granted the regular bail by the Lower Court. The offences under Section 272 and 273 of IPC, alleged against the applicant are non cognizable, thus, to bring the case of applicant under the category of cognizance offence, the authority has wrongly inserted the offence of Section 420 of IPC. The applicant has not committed any cheating with anyone and 2 MCRC-39678-2019 non of private person has made any complaint against the applicant. The ingredients of cheating is not fulfilled. the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is special enectment which specifically deals with the offence of sub standard product, thus, the penal provision of IPC do not apply in this matter. He further submits that after coming Food Rajesh Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182572831/ 1 Safety and Standards Act, 2006 into force Sections 272 and 273 of IPC are impliedly repealed , thus, no FIR can be registered under Section 272 and 273 of IPC. For the sake of argument, if it is assumed that the product of the applicant are sub standard then same is to be dealt under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Under the special act there are various kinds of violation. He has drawn attention to this Court towards Sections 42, 51, 47 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. He has also pointed out the procedure to launch the prosecution under special Act. In the present case, the procedure laid down under Food special Act are not followed and the lab report is false and arbitrary. The copy of said report has not been provided to the applicant. With the aforesaid, he prays for allowing this bail application. In support of his contention he has relied the varies judgments has mentioned as under:- 1 . Jeewan Kumar Raut and another Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in (2009) 7 SCC 526. 2. In the case of Pepsico India Holdings Private Ltd. and another Vs. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate and another reported in 2018 SCC OnLine Utt 1155 passed by High Court of Uttarakhand. 3. In the case of M/s Pepsico India Holdings (Pvt) Ltd. and another Vs. State of UP and others passed in W.P. No. 8254 (MB)/2010 passed by High Court of U.P. Per - contra, learned P.L. for the respondent/State opposes the anticipatory bail application.
